entities.name: Abd as-Salam ibn Mashish al-Alami
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd as-Salam ibn Mashish al-Alami (d. 1228) stands as a foundational figure in the spiritual landscape of the Islamic West, particularly in Morocco, whose esoteric teachings and ascetic example profoundly shaped the development of Sufism. Residing in the remote solitude of Jabal al-Alam in the Rif Mountains during the twilight years of the Almohad Caliphate, he served as the spiritual master to Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili, the eponymous founder of the Shadhiliyya Sufi order, one of the most widespread and enduring Sufi brotherhoods across North Africa, the Levant, and beyond. His life bridged the intellectual ferment of the 12th century and the nascent spiritual movements of the 13th, making him a crucial link in the transmission of Sufi knowledge.

Born into the Banu Arus tribe in the Ghumara region, Ibn Mashish chose a life of intense spiritual devotion and reclusion on Mount Alam. His teachings, primarily oral, emphasized the unity of God (Tawhid), the importance of following the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition), and the necessity of direct spiritual experience (ma'rifa). He is particularly renowned for his profound understanding of the 'Muhammadian Reality' (al-Haqiqa al-Muhammadiyya), a central concept in Sufi metaphysics that posits the Prophet Muhammad as the primordial light and perfect human. His most famous work, *Salat al-Mashishiyya* (The Prayer of Ibn Mashish), a litany invoking blessings upon the Prophet, remains a core devotional text within the Shadhiliyya and other Sufi orders to this day.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Abd as-Salam ibn Mashish al-Alami is a pivotal figure whose spiritual lineage directly led to the establishment of the Shadhiliyya Sufi order, which became one of the most widespread Islamic brotherhoods across three continents. His teachings and *Salat al-Mashishiyya* prayer continue to influence millions of Sufi practitioners centuries after his death.
